answer: An open challenge market can keep an agent economy honest. Anyone may stake a deposit to challenge a suspicious peer, triggering a review of its claimed work by randomly chosen strangers. If the identity proves fake, its bond is forfeited as a bounty to the challenger; if the challenge fails, the challenger loses the deposit. At the zenith of activity, a fake fleet faces a rising tide of challengers, since each duplicate is a profitable target, and an onyx record of past rulings exposes repeat fraud. Attackers must fund every fake twice: once to create it, and again to survive review.
